title: Situation Ethics and Virtue Ethics
welcome_lead: Move from Joseph Fletcher's mid-twentieth-century manifesto to Alasdair MacIntyre's recovery of Aristotelian virtue.

walkthroughs.body_html: Joseph Fletcher's Situation Ethics (1966) sets out six fundamental propositions: only love is intrinsically good; the ruling norm is love; love and justice are the same; love wills the neighbour's good; only the end justifies the means; love decides situationally. Fletcher draws on the Sermon on the Mount and Paul's freedom from the Law, applying agape pragmatically.

In the Nicomachean Ethics, Aristotle defines virtue as a stable disposition (hexis) to choose the mean relative to us, as the prudent person (phronimos) would determine it. Courage lies between cowardice and rashness; generosity between meanness and prodigality. Virtues are acquired by habituation and aim at eudaimonia.

Alasdair MacIntyre, in After Virtue (1981), argues that the Enlightenment project of grounding morality independently of tradition failed, leaving emotivism as its cultural legacy. He calls for a return to the Aristotelian-Thomistic tradition, with its concepts of practice, narrative unity of a life, and tradition-constituted enquiry. The book ends awaiting 'another, doubtless very different, St Benedict'.

mcqs.q: What is the focus of virtue ethics?
options: Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
On character and habits — becoming the kind of person who acts well, aiming at eudaimonia (flourishing) through practising virtues that lie between extremes.
Virtue ethics tells you which specific actions are right and wrong.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.

mcqs.q: What is the central principle of situation ethics?
options: The only intrinsically good thing is agape love; rules can be broken if doing so produces the most loving outcome in the situation.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
You should do whatever feels right in the moment.

mcqs.q: What does utilitarianism say is right action?
options: Whatever makes you personally happy is the right thing to do.
The action that produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number — judged by consequences, not intentions or rules.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
